title: The Gratitude Audit
description: Wellness night. Marigold, founder of a gratitude practice called The Reckoning, teaches that owning a thing you've thanked is ingratitude, so you must release it to the source. The source is her storage unit. Barry gets audited.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: You're listening to the Wellness Hour on Snazzie FM, and tonight, we give thanks. Our guest founded a gratitude practice called The Reckoning. Marigold, welcome.

lines.speaker: marigold
lines.text: Thank you, grateful one. <p:0.3> And thank you, listeners, for everything you are about to release.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Release? Release what?

lines.speaker: marigold
lines.text: Anything you have ever thanked, grateful one. <p:0.3> You see, if you say thank you for a thing, and then you keep it, that is not gratitude. That is greed.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Ohhh, now that is a real journey of a concept.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: That's not a journey, Ronnie, that's a... so you thank it, and then you give it away?

lines.speaker: marigold
lines.text: You release it to the source, grateful one. <p:0.3> The source receives it, so you don't have to carry the weight of owning it.

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: Last week I thanked my toaster and mailed it to the source. <p:0.3> I haven't had toast since. <p:0.3> That part is going fine.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: You mailed your toaster... where, exactly?

lines.speaker: marigold
lines.text: To the source.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: And where is the source, Marigold, for our listeners at home?

lines.speaker: marigold
lines.text: The source is a storage unit off the interstate. <p:0.3> Unit forty-one. Release it to the source.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: That's not the source. That's a storage unit with your name on it.

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: Two days ago I thanked my bed. <p:0.3> I sleep on the floor now. <p:0.3> The floor never disappointed anyone.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: The bed too? Patricia, you gave away your BED?

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Now THAT is abundance, Barry.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Abundance? My son mailed Marigold his COUCH. He gave away the couch, Ronnie. We ate Thanksgiving on the floor like raccoons.

lines.speaker: marigold
lines.text: Your son is very advanced, grateful one.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: He's not advanced, Marigold, he's sitting on a milk crate! He thanked the dining table and now it's in your unit forty-one!

lines.speaker: caller-linda
lines.text: Oh, sweetheart, no. <p:0.4> Listen to me. You can be grateful AND keep your couch. Both. At the same time.

lines.speaker: marigold
lines.text: That is the greed talking, grateful one.

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: This morning I thanked my children's winter coats. <p:0.3> They are with the source now. <p:0.3> The children are learning resilience.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: It's June, Patricia, but the COATS, you sent the kids' coats to a storage unit?

lines.speaker: caller-linda
lines.text: Sweetheart, you can be grateful AND keep your children's shoes. I am begging you. One shoe.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Linda, I think we have to respect Patricia's journey.

lines.speaker: marigold
lines.text: Now, Barry. <p:0.3> Let's do a simple exercise. Name something you are grateful for.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Uh. My apartment, I guess.

lines.speaker: marigold
lines.text: Wonderful. Release it to the source.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: What? No. I'm not releasing my apartment to unit forty-one, Marigold.

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: Last night I thanked the surgeon and released a kidney to the source.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: A KIDNEY? You put an organ in a storage unit off the interstate?

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: She gave away a KIDNEY!

lines.speaker: caller-linda
lines.text: You can be grateful AND keep your kidney, dear! That's the one I really stand by!

lines.speaker: marigold
lines.text: The source thanks you, Patricia. <p:0.3> Now, what is left, grateful one? What do you have left to release?

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: Nothing, Marigold. <p:0.3> I have nothing left. <p:0.3> I only have how grateful I feel.

lines.speaker: marigold
lines.text: Then thank the gratitude, grateful one. <p:0.4> And release it. To the source.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: You can't take her GRATITUDE, that's the only thing she has left!

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: It's at the source. <p:0.3> I feel less heavy.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: She gave away the gratitude!

lines.speaker: caller-linda
lines.text: Keep ONE thing, sweetheart!

lines.speaker: marigold
lines.text: Release it.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Don't release it!

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Where's the couch!

lines.speaker: marigold
lines.text: Unit forty-one.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Okay, everybody, calm down. <p:0.3> Wait. <p:0.3> Hold on. Where are my... where are my car keys? They were right here.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: You released them to the source, Barry. <p:0.3> Now THAT is a real journey.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: I did NOT release my keys, Ronnie, who took my keys?

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: And during the break I thanked the studio, so I went ahead and signed it over to The Reckoning. <p:0.3> We'll be right back, after a word from our new landlord.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: You signed over the... Ronnie, that's not gratitude, that's a deed!

lines.speaker: marigold
lines.text: Release it to the source, grateful one.
